purpose: copy a save into save_games as zz_<name>.save (sha-checked, zz_ names only) so `autostart campaign:zz_<name>` can load it; move every zz_ file to <state>/_to_delete afterwards; keep read-only, sha-checked copies of saves under <state>/saves

when: before every load-ladder or scenario launch of an edited save (stage), after the run (clear), and to take a copy of Liam's or a QuickSave's file out of save_games before reading or editing it (keep)
not_a_verb: a PC-side file mover with its own safety rules (zz_ prefix, sha check, nothing deleted), run in Git Bash on the PC beside job.sh

purpose: print `proxy=true|false`, `harness=true|false` and `viewer=true|false` for the files changed since a base: CI's `changes` job writes them to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and tests/test_proxy_host.py uses the proxy set to skip the proxy host tests when nothing they build from changed; an unknown base means everything changed
usage: python3 tools/changed_inputs.py --base <sha or ''>   (CI: base..HEAD) | python3 tools/changed_inputs.py --local   (merge-base with origin/main, plus staged, unstaged and untracked files); the changed files go to stderr, key=value lines to stdout
when: automatic (CI `changes` job, the `tests` gate through tests/test_proxy_host.py); by hand to see whether a branch will run the proxy, harness-windows or viewer job
not_a_verb: CI calls it before the core is checked out (the `changes` job has no submodule); a small file classifier, not a registry operation

purpose: list every failed `gates.yml` run attempt in a time window (reruns included: a rerun that passed hides its failed first attempt from `gh run list`), with the failed job and step, the first error line from its log and whether the same commit passed that job in another run (the flaky evidence), and render the committed failure table; the class and guard of each row come from CLASSES below, so a new failure is classed here, not in the generated file
usage: python3 tools/ci_failures.py --since 2026-10-29T00:00:00Z --until <utc> [--cache <json>] [--out docs/CI_FAILURES.md]   (--cache reuses a fetch; needs `gh` signed in)
when: by hand, when CI failures are reviewed (J42 built the first table); not part of any gate (it reads GitHub)
not_a_verb: a one-off report generator over the GitHub API; the table it writes is the record

purpose: post one comment on the open pull request of a branch whose CI run failed, naming each failed job and its first failed step, the run URL and which docs/CI_FAILURES.md class to check first (with the local route that reproduces it); a run that already commented (a rerun of the same attempt) is not commented again, and a branch with no open pull request gets nothing
usage: python3 tools/ci_notify.py --run-id <id> --attempt <n> --branch <head branch> [--repo owner/name] [--dry-run]   (needs `gh` with GH_TOKEN; CI's `notify` jobs in gates.yml and policy.yml run it)
when: automatic: the last job of a failed gates.yml or policy.yml run; by hand with --dry-run to see the comment a run would get
not_a_verb: CI calls it from a job without the core checkout; one GitHub API call sequence, not a registry operation

purpose: refuse three kinds of Bash or PowerShell call before they run: a `git commit` without `--trailer "Claude-Session: <this session id>"` (tools/pr_policy.py tells a job's builder from its reviewer by it), any `git` working in a protected root (both game folders, the PC state folder), and a write into a protected root outside `<state>\\_scratch\\<owner>\\` (redirects, cp/mv/rm/..., Copy-Item/Set-Content/...; pc_deploy.py and job.sh calls are exempt); each denial says what to run instead
usage: wired in .claude/settings.json (PreToolUse, matcher Bash|PowerShell); reads the hook JSON on stdin; test: echo '{"session_id":"s","cwd":"/c/x","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m x"}}' | python3 tools/claude_hook.py
when: automatic on every shell call in a Claude Code session in this repo; never run by hand except to test it
not_a_verb: Claude Code runs it with a JSON protocol on stdin and stdout, not through the wsc CLI

purpose: Refuse a pull request whose branch is not a reviewed job, a brief, a planning change or a repo-infrastructure change.
usage: python3 tools/pr_policy.py --branch <head branch> [--base origin/main]   (CI runs it on every pull request)
when: automatic in CI (`policy` job); locally before opening a pull request to see what CI will say.
not_a_verb: it reads pull-request metadata that only CI has; it becomes a core gate once warscape-core supports game gates (backlog B1).

purpose: turn a list of UI images into 2.5x master images (model x2, Lanczos to the exact size, alpha by Lanczos only, full mip chain), with a per-asset manifest, resume by input hash, and a per-asset verify

purpose: draw per-role before/after sheets at one display scale and 1:1 crops of a fixed set of hard cases (thin frames, glyph-like icons, flag cloth, portraits, cursors, soft alpha edges); 'before' is the vanilla art resampled to the same size with plain Lanczos

purpose: Check the jobs registry against jobs/ (status invariants, file links, brief shape, review rounds), pick the next job to build, review or fix, and show the queue as a readable page.
usage: python3 core/wsc.py jobs check | jobs next [--id J<n>] [--offline] | jobs review [--id J<n>] [--offline] | jobs fix [--id J<n>] [--offline] | jobs view [--offline] [--out PATH] [--no-open] | jobs view --serve [--port N] [--dry-run] [--no-open] [--auto [--interval SECONDS]]
when: `next` when Liam says "pick up the next job" (`--id` for a named job: what a session launched from the view runs); `review` for "review the next job"; `fix` for a job whose review asked for changes; `check` runs in the tests gate (CI) and before pushing a brief or a job row change; `view` to read the queue in a browser instead of registries/jobs.md, `view --serve` to start a job's brief, build, review or fix session from its button, `--auto` to start every ready review and fix by itself (D36).

purpose: check Git Bash, python3 >= 3.12, the core submodule at the pinned tag, core.hooksPath, LF shell scripts, gh auth, Docker Desktop, the empire-remastered sibling clone, Python Playwright with Chromium, the PC watcher and the PC rules (exe vanilla, no .git in or above a game folder, nothing foreign in the Napoleon folder: J18); `--fix` applies the safe fixes (a python3.exe copy, core.hooksPath)
